prayerExcerpt.en-US: He was a Christian philosopher, and excellently versed both in the profane and sacred sciences.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Era um filósofo cristão, e excelentemente versado tanto nas ciências profanas quanto nas sagradas.

cards.excerptSource: content/books/pictorial-lives-of-saints/{en-US,pt-BR}/apr-22-leonides.md, first paragraph, third sentence (the chapter has no Reflection, so the card carries none) (Pictorial Lives, public domain)
cards.subject: St. Leonides of Alexandria, half-length, in his prison: a plain Greek tunic of undyed linen and a philosopher's himation of deep slate-blue wool over his left shoulder, a plain iron fetter on each wrist joined by a short chain; in both hands, held open before him, a small unrolled papyrus letter, his son Origen's letter urging him to be constant. Behind him, a narrow stone window with iron bars and through it Alexandria in the evening: flat white roofs, a colonnaded street, the harbour with its ships and, far out on its island, the tall, stepped lighthouse of Pharos with a fire at its top, under a warm, fading sky. Steadfast and peaceful; no executioner, no sword, no lettering.
cards.face: A Greek of Alexandria of about forty-eight with a warm, light-olive complexion and a SQUARE face as wide as it is long — a FLAT, nearly VERTICAL forehead, a short, straight nose with a narrow bridge, WIDE-SET, clear grey-green eyes under THICK, STRAIGHT black brows set low, flat cheeks, a firm mouth under a DEEP groove of the upper lip, and a strong, SQUARE chin with a marked CLEFT; short, thick, black hair combed forward in a straight fringe, a very SHORT, close-cropped black beard that lets the square jaw and the cleft of the chin show; the gaze calm and level, lowered to the letter in his hands.
cards.basis: No likeness survives; Wikipedia's lead image is the Nuremberg Chronicle's Origen, not him. The book tells a Christian philosopher of Alexandria, father of seven sons, imprisoned under the prefect Laetus and beheaded in 202 after his son Origen wrote to him not to change his mind for their sakes; its engraving shows him in a prison court reading a letter, a chain at his wrist. The square face with the cleft chin is our choice, apart from `justin` and `apollonius`, the other philosopher-martyrs.

prayerExcerpt.en-US: In those stormy times of persecution Marcellinus acquired great glory.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Naqueles tempestuosos tempos de perseguição, Marcelino adquiriu grande glória.

cards.excerptSource: content/books/pictorial-lives-of-saints/{en-US,pt-BR}/apr-26-sts-cletus-and-marcellinus.md, second paragraph, second sentence (the chapter's Reflection, on the cross as the road to bliss, is about neither pope in particular) (Pictorial Lives, public domain)
cards.subject: St. Marcellinus, Bishop of Rome, half-length, as a pope of the age of Diocletian: a white tunic and a full, bell-shaped chasuble of deep crimson, a narrow white pallium with small black crosses over his shoulders; both hands holding closed against his breast a book of the Gospels in a plain, worn leather binding, kept safe in the persecution. Behind him, the Via Salaria outside Rome at dusk: a dusty road between umbrella pines and cypresses, low tombs along it, and the plain, dark doorway of the catacomb of Priscilla cut into a grassy bank, with the walls of Rome far off, under a heavy, stormy sky breaking to gold at the horizon. Grave and humble; no palm, no soldiers, no idols, no lettering.
cards.face: A Roman of about sixty-five with a pale olive complexion and a SHORT, WIDE, SOFT face — a broad, furrowed forehead running up into a BALD crown with a fringe of short grey hair, HEAVY, FLESHY upper lids half covering sorrowful dark-brown eyes, grey brows that slant UP toward the centre, a SHORT, broad nose with a rounded tip, soft, full cheeks, DEEP vertical lines from the nose past the corners of a WIDE, full-lipped mouth, a short, rounded chin; a SHORT, rounded grey beard; the gaze grave and humble, lowered a little.
cards.basis: No likeness survives; Wikipedia's lead image is a medieval miniature of his beheading, which the book does not tell. The book tells his pontificate from 296 to 304 under Diocletian, 'in those stormy times of persecution', and that he is styled a martyr though his blood was not shed; its engraving shows a pope led out between soldiers and Romans. He was buried in the catacomb of Priscilla on the Via Salaria (Wikipedia). The short, wide, soft face with the sorrowful lids is our choice, set apart from `cletus`, who shares his day and chapter (narrow, bony, forked beard).

prayerExcerpt.en-US: "Work and pray, pray and work," a voice replied, "and thou shalt be saved."
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: "Trabalha e ora, ora e trabalha", respondeu uma voz, "e serás salvo."

cards.excerptSource: content/books/pictorial-lives-of-saints/{en-US,pt-BR}/apr-27-zita.md Reflection, second sentence (Pictorial Lives, public domain)
cards.subject: St. Zita, the servant of Lucca, half-length: a plain thirteenth-century Tuscan working dress of russet-brown wool with the sleeves pushed up to the elbow, a long white linen apron, a white linen kerchief over her hair tied at the nape, a small iron ring of household keys at her belt; in her arms, gathered in a fold of the apron, fresh round loaves of bread for the poor, one hand laid over them. Behind her, Lucca: a narrow street of stone and brick houses with a tall medieval tower-house, and the plain white Romanesque front of the church of San Frediano with a band of gold mosaic high on its gable, early morning light on the stone, a clear, pale sky. Humble, cheerful and quiet; no angels, no master, no lettering.
cards.face: A Tuscan countrywoman of about forty-five with a warm, lightly sun-browned complexion and a MEDIUM OVAL face whose LOWER HALF leads in profile — a gently SLOPING forehead, a SHORT, straight nose with a small, slightly UPTURNED tip, a LONG UPPER LIP over a full, softly FORWARD mouth, a ROUNDED, firm chin, small DIMPLES in flat, narrow cheeks; LARGE, round, bright hazel eyes under straight, soft brown brows; brown hair parted in the middle under the kerchief; the gaze modest and warm, a small smile.
cards.basis: No likeness from life. The book tells her forty-eight years in the service of Fatinelli, a citizen of Lucca, her Mass before dawn, the bread made by angels while she prayed, and her charge of the household and the poor fed at the door; its engraving shows a young servant with a pitcher at a doorway. Wikipedia makes her patroness of maids and domestic servants, invoked for lost keys, and places her cult at San Frediano in Lucca, whose façade mosaic is of the thirteenth century. The oval face with the forward mouth and upturned nose is our choice.

prayerExcerpt.en-US: Thus we shall both live and die to God, perfectly resigned to His holy will in all His appointments.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Assim viveremos e morreremos para Deus, perfeitamente resignados à Sua santa vontade em todas as Suas disposições.

cards.excerptSource: content/books/pictorial-lives-of-saints/{en-US,pt-BR}/apr-28-vitalis.md Reflection, last sentence (Pictorial Lives, public domain)
cards.subject: St. Vitalis, a citizen of Milan martyred at Ravenna, half-length: a knee-length Roman tunic of dark green wool with narrow red bands, a heavy cloak of undyed grey-brown wool fastened on the right shoulder with a bronze brooch; a martyr's palm in his right hand, his left hand laid over his heart. Behind him, Ravenna in the Roman age: low brick walls and a gate, a canal with a flat boat among reeds, the flat marshy coast and a dark pine wood by the sea, and near the walls a single tall date palm, the place called the Palm-tree, under a wide, pale, luminous Adriatic sky. Resolute and serene; no rack, no pit, no stones, no judge, no lettering.
cards.face: A Milanese of about fifty with a warm, light-olive complexion and a WEDGE-SHAPED face — a BROAD, SQUARE, flat forehead and wide temples, a HEAVY, STRAIGHT brow ridge, the cheeks falling in STRAIGHT lines to a NARROW, firm chin; a long, straight nose with a strong, SQUARED tip; deep-set, level, dark-grey eyes under thick, straight dark brows; a firm, narrow mouth; short, dense, dark-brown hair cropped close, greying at the temples; a SHORT, trimmed dark beard following the narrow jaw to a blunt point; the gaze steady and resolute, toward us.
cards.basis: No likeness survives; Wikipedia's lead image is Carpaccio's altarpiece of him as a knight on a white horse. The book tells a citizen of Milan who, at Ravenna, encouraged the wavering Ursicinus to die for the faith, buried him, and was racked and buried alive at the place called the Palm-tree; its engraving shows him with a spade beside Ursicinus's body. Wikipedia calls the story a legend and holds only the martyrdom at Ravenna, of which he is the principal patron. The wedge-shaped face is our choice; the background keeps to Roman Ravenna, before the basilica built over his shrine.

prayerExcerpt.en-US: I believe in God, Creator of heaven and earth.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Creio em Deus, Criador do céu e da terra.

cards.excerptSource: content/books/pictorial-lives-of-saints/{en-US,pt-BR}/apr-29-peter.md, his own words, said as a boy and written at his death (the Reflection, on professing the faith among heretics, stays on the card) (Pictorial Lives, public domain)
cards.subject: St. Peter of Verona, Dominican friar, half-length: the white habit and white scapular of the Friars Preachers under a black cappa with its black hood laid back; in his left hand an open book held toward us, the Creed he professed; in his right, a martyr's palm. Behind him, the Lombard countryside between Como and Milan: a lonely road running through chestnut woods and green fields, a small wayside shrine, and far off the walls and towers of Milan on the plain, the snowy Alps faint on the horizon, under a bright sky with a single white cloud casting shade. Fearless and ardent; no axe, no knife, no wound, no blood, no assassins, no lettering.
cards.face: A Veronese of about forty-five, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a warm olive complexion and a COMPACT, SQUARE-ROUND head on a strong neck — a short, broad, rounded forehead, FIRM, full cheeks over a strong, ROUND, muscular jaw and a round chin with a small DIMPLE; a SHORT, straight nose; very DARK, intense, round eyes under THICK, STRAIGHT black brows that nearly MEET over the nose; a firm, full, closed mouth; thick black hair in the Dominican ring of the tonsure, the shaven cheeks blue-shadowed; the gaze fearless and ardent, toward us.
cards.basis: No likeness from life; Wikipedia's lead image is Berruguete's panel of him as a Dominican with a book. The book tells his birth at Verona of heretical parents, his answer 'I believe in God, Creator of heaven and earth', the habit from St. Dominic, his preaching in Lombardy, the cloud that shaded his hearers, and his death on the road to Milan writing the Creed in his blood; the chapter has no engraving. Wikipedia places the attack near Barlassina, on the road from Como to Milan. The compact, square-round face with the meeting brows is our choice, set apart from `thomas_aquinas`'s soft, youthful roundness.

prayerExcerpt.en-US: From his infancy he was exceedingly given to prayer and meditation, and his life was remarkably innocent and holy.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Desde a infância dava-se extremamente à oração e à meditação, e sua vida era notavelmente inocente e santa.

cards.excerptSource: content/books/pictorial-lives-of-saints/{en-US,pt-BR}/apr-29-hugh.md, first paragraph, second sentence (the chapter has no Reflection, so the card carries none; the index's reflection for 04-29 is St. Peter's) (Pictorial Lives, public domain)
cards.subject: St. Hugh, Abbot of Cluny, half-length, as an eleventh-century Benedictine abbot: a full black monastic cowl with wide sleeves and the hood laid back, a plain gold pectoral cross, an abbot's crozier of carved wood and gilt in his left hand; in his right, held against his breast, a small, closed book of the Rule. Behind him, the abbey of Cluny in its valley in Burgundy: the long Romanesque church with its many towers and bell-turrets, part of it still in building with timber scaffolding and cranes, the monastery roofs of red tile, and gentle green hills with vineyards, under a clear, golden late-afternoon sky. Noble, serene and wise; no emperor, no crown, no lettering.
cards.face: A Burgundian noble of about sixty, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a fair, lightly ruddy complexion and a SQUARE-OVAL face, full-cheeked, marked by a LONG, STRAIGHT, prominent nose that runs from a HIGH ROOT between the brows with almost no dip, like a Greek statue's; a broad, smooth forehead under the tonsure; calm, heavy-lidded grey-blue eyes set level under light, straight brows; smooth, FULL cheeks; a small, firm, closed mouth; a DEEP, rounded chin; greying fair-brown hair in a broad monastic crown; the gaze serene and noble, a little above us.
cards.basis: No likeness from life; Wikipedia's lead image is the twelfth-century miniature of Hugh with Henry IV and Matilda of Tuscany at Canossa. The book tells a prince of the house of Burgundy, professed at Cluny at sixteen under St. Odilo, abbot at twenty-five for sixty-two years, dying in 1109; its engraving shows monks in a cloister. Wikipedia and its Cluny Abbey say Hugh built the third abbey church, begun in 1089, the largest church in the world until St. Peter's. The full, square-oval face with the Greek line of the nose is our choice, apart from `hugh_grenoble`'s apple-round face and `aelred`'s soft long one.

prayerExcerpt.en-US: To serve God is to reign.

cards.excerptSource: content/books/pictorial-lives-of-saints/{en-US,pt-BR}/may-10-antoninus.md, his dying words (the Reflection, St. Augustine on almsgiving, stays on the card) (Pictorial Lives, public domain)
cards.subject: St. Antoninus, Archbishop of Florence, half-length, as a Dominican bishop of the fifteenth century: the white habit and scapular of the Friars Preachers under a black cappa, a white woollen pallium with small black crosses over his shoulders; in his right hand a round loaf held out as an alms, in his left a small pair of brass balance scales, for his just counsel; his white mitre set aside on a ledge beside him. Behind him, Florence from across the Arno: the red dome of the cathedral, the tall tower of the Palazzo Vecchio, red-tiled roofs and the old bridge with its shops, the hills of Fiesole beyond with cypresses, under a clear, soft Tuscan sky. Kind, humble and poor; no plate, no riches, no lettering.
cards.face: A small, slight Florentine of about sixty-five, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a pale olive complexion and a LARGE, HIGH, DOMED, bald cranium over a SHORT face — the face WIDEST at the cheekbones, the cheeks falling in below them; a LONG, straight, narrow nose; LARGE, ROUND, slightly prominent dark eyes under thin brows RAISED high on the forehead, which give him an attentive, listening look; deep lines from the nose to the mouth; a WIDE, THIN-LIPPED mouth; a SHORT, squared chin; a thin ring of short grey hair in the Dominican crown; the gaze attentive and kind, toward us.
cards.basis: Wikipedia's lead image, a painted portrait, shows a small, bald, clean-shaven Dominican archbishop with a long nose, raised brows and hollow cheeks, holding scales; Wikipedia gives his usual attributes as the Dominican habit, the mitre set aside and bread for the needy. The book tells 'Little Antony', named for his small stature, Archbishop of Florence from 1446 and 'the Father of the Poor'; its engraving shows him blessing among fallen men before the Palazzo Vecchio. The card keeps the portrait's features.

prayerExcerpt.en-US: Know ye that the Lord will hear your prayers, if you continue with perseverance in fastings and prayers in the sight of the Lord.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Sabei que o Senhor ouvirá vossas orações, se perseverardes constantes em jejuns e orações na presença do Senhor.

cards.excerptSource: content/books/pictorial-lives-of-saints/{en-US,pt-BR}/may-11-mammertus.md Reflection, the whole of it, the words of Judith 4:11, without the quotation marks and the reference (Pictorial Lives, public domain)
cards.subject: St. Mammertus, Bishop of Vienne, half-length, as a fifth-century Gallo-Roman bishop leading the Rogations: a white alb and a full, bell-shaped chasuble of deep violet wool; in his left hand a tall, plain processional cross of gilt bronze, his right hand raised in blessing over the fields. Behind him, a little way back and small, a long procession of clergy and people in plain cloaks walking between green fields of young wheat and vineyards, and beyond, Roman Vienne on the broad Rhône: a small Roman temple with Corinthian columns among red roofs, hills behind, a thin veil of smoke drifting away from the town under a clearing spring sky. Penitent and hopeful; no fire, no wild beasts, no lettering.
cards.face: A Gallo-Roman aristocrat of about sixty-five with a fair olive complexion and a LONG face with a CONVEX, ROMAN profile — a SLOPING forehead flowing into a LARGE, high-bridged, CURVED nose, a slightly receding upper lip and a FIRM, rounded chin; deep-set, dark-brown eyes under strong, arched grey brows; lean cheeks; grey hair cut short with a round clerical tonsure; a SHORT, neatly trimmed grey beard; the gaze earnest and pleading, lifted toward heaven.
cards.basis: No likeness survives. The book tells the calamities at Vienne, the fire quenched by his prayer and his institution of three days of fasting and supplication, the Rogations, adopted by St. Sidonius's Auvergne before 475; its engraving shows a bishop in procession under a canopy among clergy and kneeling people. Wikipedia confirms the Minor Rogations before Ascension from Sidonius and Avitus, and a family of the Lyon region. The long face with the Roman convex profile is our choice.

prayerExcerpt.en-US: God gives not the kingdom of heaven but on condition that we labor; and all we can do bears no proportion to such a crown.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Deus não dá o reino dos céus senão com a condição de que trabalhemos; e tudo o que podemos fazer não guarda proporção com tal coroa.

cards.excerptSource: content/books/pictorial-lives-of-saints/{en-US,pt-BR}/may-12-epiphanius.md, his own words, quoted in the first paragraph (the Reflection, 1 John 4:10, stays on the card) (Pictorial Lives, public domain)
cards.subject: St. Epiphanius, Bishop of Salamis in Cyprus, half-length, as a fourth-century Greek bishop who still wore the monk's habit: a plain dark-brown monastic tunic, and over it a white phelonion and a broad white omophorion with large black crosses on his shoulders; in his left hand a heavy book bound in dark leather, his work against the heresies, held closed against his side; his right hand raised in blessing. Behind him, the coast of Salamis: the blue sea and a low harbour wall, a new basilica of pale stone with a tiled roof, and the ruined columns of the older Roman city among olive trees, under a bright, hot Cypriot sky. Zealous, austere and charitable; no lettering.
cards.face: A Palestinian of about eighty-five, lean and sun-browned, with a SMALL, NARROW face of SHARP, BIRD-LIKE features under a high, POLISHED BALD dome — PINCHED temples, a THIN, SHARP, POINTED nose, SMALL, piercing, CLOSE-SET black eyes under TUFTED, bristling white brows, tight, thin lips; a LONG, straight, silver-white beard to the breast, narrow and combed; the gaze alert and searching, toward us.
cards.basis: The Painter's Manual (Hermeneia) describes 'Epiphanius of Cyprus, an old man, bald, with a white beard', and the Serbian fresco on Wikipedia shows him so, bald with a long white beard, in an omophorion with a book. The book tells his monastic life in Egypt and Palestine, his saying on labour and the crown, his election at Salamis about 367, and his zeal; its engraving shows a monk with a staff in a desert. Wikipedia's Salamis names the basilica of Bishop Epiphanius in the rebuilt city of Constantia. The small, sharp, bird-like face is our choice within that type.

prayerExcerpt.en-US: A love of Christian silence is a proof that a soul makes it her chiefest delight to be occupied on God, and finds no comfort like that of conversing with Him.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: O amor do silêncio cristão é prova de que uma alma faz da ocupação com Deus a sua maior delícia, e não encontra consolo igual ao de conversar com Ele.

cards.excerptSource: content/books/pictorial-lives-of-saints/{en-US,pt-BR}/may-13-john-the-silent.md Reflection, first sentence (Pictorial Lives, public domain)
cards.subject: St. John the Silent, monk of the laura of St. Sabas, half-length: a coarse black monastic habit and a black hood drawn over his head, a leather belt; his hands folded quietly on his breast over a small wooden cross on a cord. Behind him, the deep, dry gorge of the Kidron in the Judaean desert: tawny cliffs with small monks' cells and a little church built into the rock on terraces, a few palms far below, and high in the clear evening sky a soft, bright cross of light. Silent and recollected, his lips closed; no bishop's vestments, no lettering.
cards.face: An Armenian of about seventy-five with a pale olive complexion and a BROAD-TEMPLED face — a WIDE, HIGH forehead and broad temples, DEEP eye sockets in which LARGE, dark, heavy-lidded eyes rest LOWERED and half closed in recollection, a LONG, strong nose with a gentle HUMP and a tip that points DOWNWARD, LOW, broad cheekbones, a small mouth gently pressed shut; thin white hair under the hood; a LONG, full white beard that widens toward the bottom and ends SQUARE; the gaze inward and still, lowered.
cards.basis: The Menologion of Basil II (Wikipedia's lead image) shows him as an old monk in a dark habit with a white beard, kneeling before the laura. The book tells his noble birth at Nicopolis in Armenia, his monastery at eighteen, his nine years as Bishop of Colonia, the bright cross that led him to St. Sabas, his hidden life there and forty years in his cell; its engraving shows a monk drawing water at a well. The broad-templed face with the deep-set, lowered eyes is our choice, apart from `john_climacus`'s lean, bony rectangle.
